metadata.title: Round 4: branches and office families, Crown corporations, the regional health system, hospital districts and the health statutes

conventions.date_precision: kept as stated by the source; a year is never 1 January

events.title: Sheriff's Act, 1860 proclaimed in the Colony of British Columbia, regulating the office of High Sheriff

evidence.locator: Proclamation, PDF pp. 1-2, ss. 1-4 and issuing clause ('this eighth day of March ... 1860')

events.interpretation_notes: A colonial predecessor of the provincial sheriffs: it regulates the mainland High Sheriff (naming the late Charles Samuel Nicol and the present Peter O'Reilly) and temporary appointments by a judge. It does not create county offices and is not the start of today's Sheriff Service.

events.title: Sheriffs Act, 1873 authorizes sheriffs for Vancouver Island, the City of New Westminster and Cariboo

evidence.locator: Official historical compilation, chapter 146, printed p. 648 / PDF p. 1, s. 1; s. 16 at printed pp. 651-652 / PDF pp. 4-5

events.interpretation_notes: Authority to appoint, not the first appointments. The text read is a later official compilation, not the original sessional chapter. Section 16 requires monthly sworn accounts of fines, penalties and forfeitures to the Minister of Finance and Agriculture: a financial-reporting duty, not proof that Finance administered the sheriffs.

events.title: Sheriffs Act amendment of 1878 authorizes separate sheriffs for Nanaimo, Kootenay and Cassiar

evidence.locator: 1878 c. 17, printed p. 75 / PDF p. 1, ss. 1-2

events.interpretation_notes: Appointment authority and territorial adjustments to the Vancouver Island and New Westminster bailiwicks; the first appointees are not identified.

events.title: Sheriffs and Registrars Act, 1880 provides for a sheriff for the Clinton Judicial District
events.interpretation_notes: Assent only: the sections creating the Clinton bailiwick take effect by proclamation (s. 8), which was not recovered. The 1888 Act shows a Sheriff for the Clinton Judicial District in office by then.

events.title: Six sheriffs continued under county titles: Vancouver Island becomes Victoria, City of New Westminster becomes Westminster, Clinton Judicial District becomes Yale, and Kootenay, Nanaimo and Cariboo become counties of those names

evidence.locator: Sheriffs Amendment Act 1888, c. 33, printed pp. 103-104 / PDF pp. 1-2, ss. 1-3 ('shall, on the passage of this Act, respectively, be the Sheriff for the County of ...')

events.interpretation_notes: Continuation and renaming of existing offices on the Act's passage, not six new offices. Section 3 hands the Cassiar sheriff's pending writs to the Sheriff for Nanaimo, whose county now includes Cassiar: a transfer of specified work, not an asset transfer.

events.title: Sheriffs Act Amendment Act, 1892 provides for a Sheriff for the County of Vancouver, taking its territory out of Westminster
events.interpretation_notes: Assent; s. 5 leaves commencement to an order in council, which was not found.

events.title: Thomas Joseph Armstrong appointed Acting Sheriff for the County of Vancouver

evidence.locator: OIC 427/1892, PDF pp. 1, 4; approval date 26 October 1892 cross-referenced in OIC 241/1893, p. 1

events.interpretation_notes: An appointment that shows a Vancouver sheriff office operating by this day; not proved to be the first.

events.title: James Deacon Hall appointed Sheriff for the County of Vancouver; the acting appointment cancelled

evidence.locator: OIC 241/1893, PDF p. 3 (signed order, Government House, 3 July)

events.interpretation_notes: The year on the signed order is read as 1893 from the scan and the order number; the OCR reads 1897.

events.title: Counties Definition Act, 1895 set to come into force, replacing the separate court and sheriff districts with common counties

evidence.locator: OIC 346/1895, approved 2 September 1895, PDF pp. 1-2; Act (R4B-046) printed pp. 33-34, ss. 5, 8, 10

events.interpretation_notes: The commencement day fixed by the order; the Gazette proclamation was not retrieved. The Act changes territory and continues officers without reappointment: it does not create new sheriff offices.

events.title: County of Atlin defined from the territory of the County of Vancouver
events.interpretation_notes: The day fixed for the 1903-04 Act to come into force (assent 10 February 1904 is not commencement); the proclamation was not retrieved. County creation, not a sheriff appointment.

events.title: References to the County of Atlin become references to the County of Prince Rupert

evidence.locator: Counties Definition Amendment Act 1920, c. 20, printed p. 75 / PDF p. 1, ss. 1-3 ('Assented to 17th April, 1920')

events.interpretation_notes: Assent; the Act has no delayed-commencement clause. A county-name bridge, not the first Prince Rupert sheriff. It explains the 'County of Prince Rupert' bailiwick in the 1972-73 roster already held.

events.title: Sheriff Services observed as one of three services administered by the Director of Court Services, with regional sheriffs reporting to the managers of six justice regions

evidence.locator: Taskforce on Municipal Policing Costs in British Columbia, Preliminary Report (July 1978), Appendix 12, section D, printed p. 356 / PDF p. 242

events.interpretation_notes: A bounded 1978 observation from a provincial task-force report, not the 1974 consolidation instrument. The report cites the May 1977 Report of the Task Force on Sheriff Services and the September 1977 Sheriff Services Program Inventory and Review (Court Services, Ministry of the Attorney General) as sources (printed pp. 352-353); neither was recovered.

events.title: Arms, supporters, flag and badge granted to the Sheriff Service

evidence.locator: Public Register of Arms, Flags and Badges, project 2209, vol. VI p. 64

events.interpretation_notes: The grant date; the Canada Gazette announcement was 24 March 2012. Not a founding date and not the first use of any sheriff logo.

events.title: OIC 1930/1978 charges the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing with the administration of the Urban Transit Authority Act

evidence.locator: OIC 1930/1978, operative paragraph; approval stamp 13 July 1978

events.interpretation_notes: Order made (approved) 13 July 1978, a week before the corporation existed. It is express statute-assignment evidence, the basis of the UTA responsibility period proposed from 20 July 1978; it is not the body's start.

events.title: Urban Transit Authority of British Columbia established: section 2 of the Urban Transit Authority Act in force

evidence.locator: OIC 1931/1978 (approved 13 July 1978), operative paragraph bringing ss. 1-5, 8-20, 22-24 and 25(1) into force on 20 July 1978; Act s. 2 (R4E-003)

events.interpretation_notes: In-force date of the establishing section, by proclamation ordered 13 July 1978. Assent was 29 June 1978 (already held as atlas:uta-act-assent-1978). Sections 6, 7, 21 and 25(2) were not commenced by this order. Supersedes the organisation-reported 1979 (atlas:uta-created-1979) as the legal start.

events.title: Directors of the Urban Transit Authority (at least eight) to be appointed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council from persons holding elected municipal office

evidence.locator: Urban Transit Authority Act, SBC 1978 c. 39, s. 4; in force 20 July 1978 under OIC 1931/1978

events.interpretation_notes: An appointment relation (G3), not a line of accountability: the directors' municipal office does not make the Authority answerable to municipalities or electors. Dated from the provision's commencement.

events.title: Metro Transit Operating Company established: the Metro Transit Operating Company Act in force

evidence.locator: OIC 29/1980 (approved 10 January 1980), operative paragraph; Act s. 2 and s. 17 (R4E-006)

events.interpretation_notes: In force by proclamation on 18 January 1980. The 31 July 1979 assent (atlas:mtoc-act-assent-1979) is not the start. Commencement does not date the transfer of Hydro transit employees or property, which the Act provided for separately and which remains undated here.

events.title: Directors of the Metro Transit Operating Company (at least seven) to be appointed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council

evidence.locator: Metro Transit Operating Company Act, SBC 1979 c. 18, s. 4; in force 18 January 1980 (OIC 29/1980)

events.interpretation_notes: An appointment relation (G3), not an accountability line.

events.title: The Urban Transit Authority becomes British Columbia Transit: Urban Transit Authority Amendment Act, 1982 in force

evidence.locator: OIC 1534/1982 (approval stamp 12 August 1982); Act SBC 1982 c. 53, ss. 1 and 3 (R4E-008); 1991 consolidation s. 2 historical note (R4E-018) gives 12 August 1982

events.interpretation_notes: The same corporation continues under a new name; it is not a new incorporation. The order itself prints no separate in-force day; 12 August 1982 rests on its approval and the official consolidation's note. Narrows atlas:uta-renamed-bctransit-1982 (year) and supplies the proclamation date atlas:uta-amendment-1982-assent says was not found. The 1983 "merger" date is not supported.

events.title: British Columbia Transit expressly made an agent of the Crown by the replacement establishing section

evidence.locator: Urban Transit Authority Amendment Act, 1982, s. 3 (replacement s. 2(1)); in force 12 August 1982 (OIC 1534/1982)

events.interpretation_notes: Crown agency is a legal status, not a ministry line. The claim is about the express clause; it does not say the Authority had no Crown status before.

events.title: Property and rights of the Metro Transit Operating Company vested in British Columbia Transit, which becomes liable for its debts and obligations

evidence.locator: OIC 1093/1985 (approved 30 May 1985) bringing the British Columbia Transit Amendment Act (No. 2), 1985 into force on 1 June 1985; new s. 2.1 of the Transit Act (R4E-012, s. 2)

events.interpretation_notes: A transfer and assumption, not a dissolution: the provision does not dissolve MTOC, and OIC 1096/1985 appointed a new MTOC board effective the same day. Assent was 24 May 1985; the order's 30 May approval is not the transfer date.

events.title: Metro Transit Operating Company employees transferred to British Columbia Transit

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1984/85 as reproduced in the Auditor General's 1986 report, note 18(e), printed B21; OIC 1094/1985 (R4E-014) selecting every MTOC employee under new s. 6.1

events.interpretation_notes: June 1 is stated by the Public Accounts and matches the commencement of the enabling section. OIC 1094 says only "the effective date of this order"; its 30 May approval is not the transfer date.

events.title: OIC 1096/1985 appoints nine directors of the Metro Transit Operating Company, with Stuart Milton Hodgson as chair, effective 1 June 1985

evidence.locator: OIC 1096/1985, operative paragraph ("effective June 1, 1985"); OIC 1095/1985 (R4E-015) appoints the parallel BC Transit board

events.interpretation_notes: Positive evidence that MTOC continued as a legal entity after its assets and employees passed to BC Transit. Its legal end is not established.

events.title: OIC 3495/1976 charges the Minister of Consumer and Corporate Affairs with the administration of the Liquor Distribution Act

evidence.locator: OIC 3495/1976, operative paragraph; approved 2 December 1976

events.interpretation_notes: Order made before the Act's 31 December 1976 commencement; the proposed responsibility period starts on commencement. The companion OIC 3491/1976 assigned the Liquor Control and Licensing Act to the same minister (not applied: that branch is not an atlas body).

events.title: Liquor Distribution Act in force: section 2 establishes the Liquor Distribution Branch by statute and existing government liquor stores continue under it

evidence.locator: OIC 3494/1976 (approved 2 December 1976), operative paragraph, in force 31 December 1976 except ss. 16(3) and 17(1); Act s. 2 (R4E-020); 1991 consolidation historical note (R4E-027)

events.interpretation_notes: Statutory establishment of the branch under this name. It does not date when the 1973 Liquor Administration Branch began to be called the Liquor Distribution Branch administratively (E9, still open); the body keeps its 1973 start. Supplies the in-force date atlas:ldb-act-assent-1975 says was not found.

events.title: The budgets of the Liquor Distribution Branch and the Liquor Control and Licensing Branch are separated

evidence.locator: Hansard, 1 September 1977, answer of Hon. K.R. Mair to question 97, pp. 5210-5211

events.interpretation_notes: A financial separation stated by the responsible minister later in 1977; distinct from the 1975 assent and the 31 December 1976 commencement. Not an establishment date for either branch.

events.title: Government Liquor Act and Liquor-control Plebiscites Act repealed

evidence.locator: OIC 3493/1976 (approved 2 December 1976), operative paragraph; Liquor Distribution Act s. 27 (R4E-020)

events.interpretation_notes: Repeal of the Board's 1921 statute. It is not a dissolution order for the Liquor Control Board and does not move the body's 1973 end (functions split in 1973 per BC Archives; see atlas:lcb-replaced-gla-1973-assent).

events.title: British Columbia Hydro and Power Authority Act (1962) in force by proclamation, amalgamating the Power Commission and BC Electric as BC Hydro

evidence.locator: OIC 839/1962 (approved 30 March 1962): proclamation bringing the Act into force "on the 30th day of March, 1962"; Act s. 3(1), s. 28 (R4E-030)

events.interpretation_notes: The original statutory amalgamation took effect on 30 March 1962, not 31 March (the BC Archives date the body currently carries) and not the 29 March assent. The scheme was held ultra vires on 29 July 1963 and rebuilt in 1964-65; it remains the historical start of the Hydro lineage. Corroborates atlas:hydro-enacted-1962-03-30 (BC Hydro's own timeline) with the original order.

events.title: OIC 840/1962 appoints the first directors of BC Hydro, with Gordon M. Shrum and Hugh L. Keenleyside as co-chairmen

evidence.locator: OIC 840/1962, appointment paragraphs; approved 30 March 1962

events.interpretation_notes: Order-approval date under the original 1962 scheme. Gives a documented start for the co-chairmanship that atlas:hydro-cochairs-1960s only bounds to "the 1960s"; their end dates are not supplied.

events.title: Chief Justice Lett holds the Power Development Act, 1961, its 1962 amendment and the 1962 Hydro Act ultra vires

evidence.locator: BC Hydro second annual report, year ended 31 March 1964, printed p. 17 (PDF p. 19) and financial note 1, printed p. 22 (PDF p. 24)

events.interpretation_notes: Reported by Hydro's own contemporary annual report; the judgment itself was not retrieved, and no appellate outcome is asserted (the action was settled on 27 September 1963).

events.title: Settlement agreement with British Columbia Power Corporation over the BC Electric shares; total compensation $197,114,358

evidence.locator: BC Hydro second annual report, printed p. 17 and note 1, printed p. 22; ratified by the Power Measures Act, 1964 (R4E-038)

events.interpretation_notes: Agreement date. Separate from the 1961 vesting (already held as atlas:hydro-pda-1961-vesting) and the 1965 amalgamation.

events.title: British Columbia Electric Company Limited Acquisition Act assented: acquisition of all common shares authorized as at 1 August 1961

evidence.locator: SBC 1964 c. 6, assent heading and ss. 2-3

events.interpretation_notes: Enacted 20 March 1964 with retroactive effect to 1 August 1961; the body's 1961-08-01 start is the deemed date and stays.

events.title: British Columbia Hydro and Power Authority Act, 1964 in force: the Authority constituted anew as a Crown agent, with the Minister of Finance as fiscal agent and directors appointed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council

evidence.locator: OIC 2519/1964, recital 4 (the Act "came into force and effect on the Proclamation" of 23 March 1964); OIC 773/1964 (R4E-036); Act ss. 3-6, 58 (R4E-035)

events.interpretation_notes: The legal constitution of the present Authority after the 1963 judgment. Drawn as a change of legal basis, not a new body: the lineage starts in 1962. Crown agency, fiscal agency and appointment are typed relations; "Finance is fiscal agent" is not a ministry-responsibility period (the responsible-3 gap for 1962-1964 stands).

events.title: OIC 2386/1965 authorizes the amalgamation of the 1964 Authority, British Columbia Electric Company Limited and the British Columbia Power Commission

evidence.locator: OIC 2386/1965, pp. 1-2; approved 20 August 1965

events.interpretation_notes: Authorizing order; the agreement it calls for fixes the effective time (next event).

events.title: BC Electric and the BC Power Commission amalgamate with the 1964 Authority and cease their separate corporate existence (5 p.m. Vancouver time)

evidence.locator: Power Measures Act, 1966 (SBC 1966 c. 38), s. 3, s. 5 and Schedule clauses 1-2, printed pp. 241-242

events.interpretation_notes: Effective 5 p.m. local time, Friday 20 August 1965, under the agreement of that day, which continues the three as the Authority established by the 1964 Act. Section 5 deems the Crown-held BC Electric common shares surrendered and cancelled on the amalgamation. The 1966 Act (assented 1 April 1966) ratified it; its assent is not the amalgamation date. This is the proposed end of both predecessor records.

events.title: OIC 2387/1965 revokes and cancels the incorporation of British Columbia Electric Company Limited and declares it dissolved

evidence.locator: OIC 2387/1965, operative paragraph; approved 23 August 1965

events.interpretation_notes: A formal Companies Act cancellation after the fact: the order recites that the company had already ceased separate existence on amalgamation (20 August). It does not move the end.

events.title: The Housing Fund holds all three issued common shares of Pemco Holdings Ltd. (cost $633,511)

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1975/76, printed B10, Housing Fund investment schedule (columns for 31 March 1975 and 31 March 1976)

events.interpretation_notes: An observation at two balance-sheet dates (31 March 1975 and 31 March 1976), not the 1973 purchase day or instrument, and not a ministry period: a fund's holding is ownership, not accountability.

events.title: Special resolution to change the name of Pemco Holdings Ltd. to British Columbia Housing Corporation

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1975/76, printed F154, note 5 (subsequent event)

events.interpretation_notes: Resolution date. The name took effect with the Registrar's certificate of 7 May 1976, which the body's names already use; the resolution does not replace it.

events.title: British Columbia Steamship Company (1975) Ltd. incorporated under the Canada Corporations Act to operate the Princess Marguerite

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1975/76, printed F84, note 1(a); audited statements from printed F80

events.interpretation_notes: Incorporation date as stated in the company's first audited statements; the federal certificate was not obtained.

events.title: The company acquires British Columbia Steamship Company Inc., a Washington corporation used for liquor sales aboard the vessel in that state

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1975/76, printed F84, note 1(a)

events.interpretation_notes: Two companies: the Washington subsidiary is a separate legal entity and is not drawn.

events.title: The company's five issued shares are held by its five directors in right of the Province

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1975/76, printed F81 (balance sheet) and F84 note 1(a)

events.interpretation_notes: Beneficial provincial ownership observed at the statement date. It is not personal ownership by the directors, and it does not name a responsible ministry (the E1 gap for this company stands).

events.title: BC Rail's $15.5 million purchase of Vancouver Wharves is raised in the Legislature as already made

evidence.locator: Hansard, 30 March 1993 (afternoon), Oral Questions, "B.C. Rail Purchase of Vancouver Wharves Ltd." (D. Symons; Hon. A. Charbonneau)

events.interpretation_notes: A latest date: the purchase was complete on or before 30 March 1993. Not the closing day (a 25 March 1993 secondary date is held, not applied). The Hansard says "B.C. Rail"; whether the buyer was the Company or its operating subsidiary BC Rail Ltd. is not stated. Vancouver Wharves is not an atlas body.

events.title: Ministerial Order 5/2004 approves the BC Rail reorganization, including transfer of BC Rail Ltd.'s 75% interest in Vancouver Wharves Limited Partnership to the Company or an affiliate

evidence.locator: Ministerial Order 5/2004, Railway Certificate 6497, signed 30 December 2003; Schedule A(j) and Schedule B

events.interpretation_notes: An approval of described transactions, not proof of closing. The interest is in a limited partnership, not shares of a company. The order's 2004 number does not change its 2003 signature date.

events.title: Harbour Board Repeal Act assented; its repeal and dissolution sections await commencement by regulation

evidence.locator: Harbour Board Repeal Act, SBC 1983 c. 5, assent heading, ss. 2, 3 and 8

events.interpretation_notes: Assent is not the dissolution: ss. 2-3 needed an order (next event). Sections 4-5 provide for transfers of assets and liabilities to BC Development Corporation and BC Railway Company on dates Cabinet fixes; those orders are not in this package.

events.title: British Columbia Harbours Board dissolved and its members' appointments terminated on repeal of the Harbour Board Act

evidence.locator: OIC 1061/1985 (approved 30 May 1985) bringing ss. 2 and 3 of the Harbour Board Repeal Act into force "by this regulation"; confirmed 30 May 1985 by Public Accounts 1984/85, printed C24, note 19(b) (R4E-017)

events.interpretation_notes: Dissolution in force. It is not the date of the asset transfers under ss. 4-5, which remain undated.

events.title: Regional health boards and community health councils added to FOIPPA's "health care body" class, in force on assent

evidence.locator: SBC 1995 c. 53 (Miscellaneous Statutes Amendment Act (No. 3), 1995), PDF p. 1 / printed p. 925 (assented to July 13, 1995), PDF p. 4 / printed p. 928 s. 14 (Schedule 1, "health care body", new paras. (g) and (h)), PDF p. 22 / printed p. 946 s. 55 (s. 14 not among the provisions deferred to regulation)

events.interpretation_notes: A class date, not a creation date. Section 14 adds boards designated under Health Authorities Act s. 4(1) and councils designated under s. 6(1) to the FOIPPA Schedule 1 definition of health care body; it commenced on Royal Assent (the official 1995 Table of Statutes, root source R4R-081, PDF p. 80, lists the amendment without a deferred date; the RS1996 FOIPPA historical table cites 1995-53-14, R4H-018 PDF pp. 37, 55). Related subjects are the boards and councils the atlas holds as designated by that day; for each, coverage starts no earlier than both this day and its own designation, and later-designated bodies enter on designation. It does not cover the community health services societies of 1997, is distinct from the 3 November 1994 hospital and regional-hospital-district class date (root module), and is a scrutiny relation, not ministry accountability. The original Health Authorities Act 1993 c. 47 made no FOIPPA amendment (R4H-017, s. 18 is its only consequential amendment). The April 1997 FOIPPA dates belong to the Hospital Appeal Board name in Schedule 2, not to this class.

events.title: The Pacific Organ Retrieval for Transplantation program is described as funded by the Ministry of Health

evidence.locator: Hansard, 27 April 1987 afternoon sitting, printed p. 787, statement of Minister Dueck (Organ Donor Awareness Week)

events.interpretation_notes: An observation of a program on that day, filed under BC Transplant's lineage because the atlas has no program node. Funding is not ownership or accountability and is not drawn as a line. The same passage says the program "coordinates organ retrieval efforts with the B.C. Heart Transplant Society", a name not otherwise in the atlas; the Corporate Registry shows the British Columbia Transplant Society (S0021154) from 1 April 1986. This is not a start date for the program or the society.

events.title: The Health minister describes PORT as a program the B.C. Transplant Society initiated, coordinating organ retrieval across the province

evidence.locator: Hansard, 27 April 1988 afternoon sitting, printed p. 4096, statement of Minister Dueck

events.interpretation_notes: Program-to-society relationship observed on that day: PORT is described as a program the society initiated and the Ministry of Health funds. This does not make PORT a former registered name of the society or date a rename. The same passage says the government and medical community established the society in 1985; that is kept as a competing establishment claim beside the 1 April 1986 registration (sub-agency batch), not as an event.

events.title: The Health minister dates the Pacific organ retrieval program to 1985

evidence.locator: Hansard, 9 June 1988 morning sitting (Ministry of Health estimates), printed p. 4951, statement of Minister Dueck; the online text renders the acronym "PORF"

events.interpretation_notes: A retrospective, attributed year for a program, reported in 1988. It is not the founding of BC Transplant or of the British Columbia Transplant Society, whose registry registration is 1 April 1986 (atlas:primary-evidence-transplant-society-1986). No day or legal instrument is known.

events.title: A research article describes the Pacific Organ Retrieval for Transplantation System as part of the British Columbia Transplant Society

evidence.locator: A. M. J. Buchan, J Clin Invest 87 (April 1991), printed p. 1382, Methods, Cell isolation; DOI 10.1172/JCI115143

events.interpretation_notes: An independent, non-government observation of the program as part of the society, dated by the issue month. Not evidence of a corporate rename or of when the relationship began.

events.title: Oak Bay Lodge Society's assets pass to the new OBL Continuing Care Society, its land and building to the Vancouver Island Health Authority

evidence.locator: Vancouver Island Health Authority, consolidated financial statements 2004/05 (Public Accounts 2004/05, supplement E), PDF p. 7 / printed p. 5, note 1
evidence.url_basis: R3H-069: Round 3 source register not in the handback; URL recovered and passage re-read by the integrator on 2026-10-21 (PDF p. 7 note 1)

events.interpretation_notes: Effective day of the transfer under a Distribution Agreement made 31 March 2004 between Oak Bay Lodge Society, the Authority and OBL Continuing Care Society. The new society was incorporated on 20 February 2004 and began operating on 1 April 2004. The Authority controls it because it appoints its board; that is a board-appointment relation, not ownership. A 2004 example of the society-to-authority transfers A7 asks about, not one of the 1997 transfers.

events.title: Schedule B of the Regional Health Boards Regulation, which describes the health authorities' regions, is replaced (B.C. Reg. 8/2003)

evidence.locator: 2003 cumulative regulation bulletin, Health Authorities Act: M9/2003, amending B.C. Reg. 293/2001, B.C. Reg. 8/2003, January 17/03; order text at https://www.bclaws.gov.bc.ca/civix/document/id/mo/hmo/m0009_2003
evidence.url_basis: R3H-106: Round 3 source register not in the handback; URL recovered and passage re-read by the integrator on 2026-10-21 (Health Authorities Act row)

events.interpretation_notes: The deposit day. M9/2003 (Minister of Health Services) repeals Schedule B and substitutes a new one; the order's signing day is not read, and its "December 6, 2002" footer is a drafting mark, not a date of effect. Which boundaries changed is not compared here. Regions are areas, not bodies; HSDAs are not described in Schedule B.

events.title: A parcel at 3405 Willingdon Avenue, Burnaby (the Burnaby Centre for Mental Health and Addictions) moved from Fraser Health's region to Vancouver Coastal Health's

evidence.locator: M158/2008, p. 1 clauses (a)-(c) amending Schedule B ss. 1 and 5 of B.C. Reg. 293/2001; date line "June 25/08"; Schedule C (PID 018-811-337, Parcel A)
evidence.url_basis: R3H-067: Round 3 source register not in the handback; URL recovered and passage re-read by the integrator on 2026-10-21 (p. 1 clauses (a)-(c), date line, Schedule C)

events.interpretation_notes: The day the order was signed. The handback reports deposit as B.C. Reg. 162/2008 on 27 June 2008 (R3HC-068, Gazette; not re-read here). Only this parcel moves. Reading s. 1 as Fraser's region and s. 5 as Vancouver Coastal's follows the handback.

events.title: The British Columbia Provincial Renal Agency is listed among the health entities PHSA was formed from, in its statements for the year to 31 March 2002

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 2002/03, Summary of audited financial statements of public bodies reporting under the Financial Information Act, for the year ended 31 March 2002, PDF p. 5 footnote 5
evidence.url_basis: R3H-072: Round 3 source register not in the handback; URL recovered and passage re-read by the integrator on 2026-10-21 (PDF p. 5 footnote 5)

events.interpretation_notes: The end of a reporting period, not a transfer day. The footnote reads "amalgamated from previously existing health entities". It is a summary label, not the instrument, so it narrows B1 (the agency sat within PHSA by 31 March 2002) without settling December 2001 against 2002.

events.title: PHSA's 2004/05 statements list the provincial agencies and programs it directly manages and governs

evidence.locator: PHSA consolidated financial statements, years ended 31 March 2005 and 2004 (Public Accounts 2004/05, supplement E), PDF p. 7 / printed p. 5, note 1
evidence.url_basis: R3H-071: Round 3 source register not in the handback; URL recovered and passage re-read by the integrator on 2026-10-21 (PDF p. 7 note 1; PDF p. 12 note 5 (image-only PDF, read visually))

events.interpretation_notes: A checkpoint at the end of the fiscal year, not a founding date. The list: BC Cancer Agency Branch; BC Centre for Disease Control and Prevention Society Branch; BC Drug and Poison Information Centre; BC Mental Health Society (Riverview) Branch; BC Provincial Renal Agency; BC Transplant Society Branch; Cardiac Services; Children's & Women's Health Centre of BC Branch; Forensic Psychiatric Services Commission; Red Cross Outpost Hospitals. Legal forms differ (branch societies, a commission, programs). Related subjects are the atlas sub-agencies these correspond to; the poison centre, FPSC and outpost hospitals have no atlas id.

events.title: The Province grants the Oak Street land and premises to the Children's & Women's Health Centre of British Columbia Branch

evidence.locator: PHSA consolidated financial statements 2004/05, PDF p. 12 / printed p. 10, note 5 (continued)
evidence.url_basis: R3H-071: Round 3 source register not in the handback; URL recovered and passage re-read by the integrator on 2026-10-21 (PDF p. 7 note 1; PDF p. 12 note 5 (image-only PDF, read visually))

events.interpretation_notes: An asset grant, subject to Hospital Act s. 48 restrictions on alteration, lease and transfer. Separate from the 1997 amalgamation and the 2001 branch society.

events.title: Three corporations designated as hospitals, and the Children's and Women's Health Centre of British Columbia to be designated on amalgamation (M249/1997)

evidence.locator: M249/1997 (Hospital Act s. 1), clauses 1-2; "This Order made the 24 day of June, 1997"
evidence.url_basis: R3H-073: Round 3 source register not in the handback; URL recovered and passage re-read by the integrator on 2026-10-21 (clauses 1-2 and date line)

events.interpretation_notes: The order names British Columbia's Children's Hospital, "British Columbia's Hospital and Health Centre Society" (as printed, without "Women's") and Sunny Hill Health Centre for Children, and provides that the new society will be designated "upon amalgamation". It anticipates the amalgamation of 15 July 1997 (atlas:primary-evidence event, S0037131). It is not the certificate and does not prove the complete participant list.

events.title: Women's Institute Hospital Association for Crippled Children registered as a society (S0001435), later British Columbia's Children's Hospital

evidence.locator: BC Corporate Registry credential history via OrgBook BC, credential 3067628 (Event:CONVSCREGI)

events.title: OIC 1222/1967 divides the Province into 27 areas for regional hospital districts under section 3 of the Regional Hospital Districts Act (SBC 1967 c.43)

evidence.locator: OIC 1222/1967, approved and ordered 13 April 1967; recital of s.3 and schedule of areas 1-27 (PDF pp. 1-3); recommended by the acting Minister of Health Services and Hospital Insurance (signature block, PDF p. 3)

events.interpretation_notes: The day the order defining the areas was approved. It is not a common incorporation date: each district was incorporated later by its own letters patent (the 28 originals recovered run from 29 June 1967, Greater Vancouver, to 8 October 1968, Squamish-Lillooet). The department recommended the order; the districts are local corporations with their own boards, not branches of the department, and are not drawn as bodies.

events.title: OIC 3082/1969 dissolves 23 hospital improvement districts incorporated under the Water Act and transfers all their assets, rights, claims, obligations and liabilities to the regional hospital district paired with each

evidence.locator: OIC 3082/1969, approved and ordered 25 September 1969; recitals, operative recommendation under s.50C of the Regional Hospital Districts Act, and Schedule columns A-B; recommended by the Minister of Health Services and Hospital Insurance

events.interpretation_notes: The order recites that the hospital fund-raising functions of the improvement districts had been assigned to the regional hospital districts. Dissolution and transfer take effect by the order itself. The 23 districts were incorporated by letters patent between 7 August 1951 (Creston Valley) and 23 April 1964 (Kelowna and District); this is the recovered set, not a census of every hospital improvement district. Fort Nelson (13 June 1972) and 100 Mile House (12 May 1972) were dissolved by later orders and are not part of this one.

events.title: OIC 527/1972 amends the letters patent of 28 regional hospital districts so that their municipal membership, electoral areas and voting units follow the corresponding municipal regional districts

The recitals describe boards of corresponding regional directors; each district's first board is in its own letters patent.

events.title: OIC 1549/1995 limits 24 regional hospital districts, from 31 December 1995, to completing minister-approved capital projects, paying their debt, requisitioning and any other power the minister approves

events.title: Twelve new regional hospital districts incorporated by letters patent: Cariboo, Central Vancouver Island, Coast Garibaldi, East Kootenay, Northern Interior, North Okanagan, North West, Peace Liard, South Okanagan Similkameen, Thompson, Upper Island/Central Coast and West Kootenay-Boundary

evidence.locator: OIC 1550/1995 to OIC 1561/1995 (one order per district), each approved 14 December 1995; final clause of each letters patent ("The effective date of these Letters Patent is January 1, 1996"). URL is OIC 1550/1995 (Cariboo); the other eleven are at arc_oic/1551_1995 to 1561_1995

events.interpretation_notes: Incorporation in force 1 January 1996; 14 December 1995 is the approval day, not the start. The new Cariboo, East Kootenay and North Okanagan districts are separate corporations from the 1967-68 districts of the same names, which continued under the 1995 restriction. Several share names with regional health boards of 1994-95 (Northern Interior, Thompson, Central Vancouver Island and others); a hospital district is not a health board, and no identity is drawn between them.

events.title: OIC 1429/1998 repeals the 1995 restriction for 13 older regional hospital districts, orders five of the 1996 districts dissolved on 31 December 1998 with their assets divided among named districts, and continues Cariboo-Coast as Cariboo-Chilcotin and Coast Garibaldi as Sea to Sky with smaller territory

evidence.locator: OIC 1429/1998, approved and ordered 19 November 1998; Schedule A ss.1,3,4,7-12,16,18,19,21 (restrictions repealed), ss.5,15,17,20,22 (dissolutions and transfers), ss.2 and 6 (renames and partial transfers), ss.13,14,23 (membership and boundaries)

events.interpretation_notes: The day of the order. Restored powers are not new incorporations. Transfers had to be completed by 31 December 1998, and the schedule makes vesting depend on each actual transfer; the closing days are not recovered. The renames take effect immediately. OIC 1430/1998 separately incorporated the Stuart-Nechako Regional Hospital District on the same day.

events.title: OIC 1601/1998 dissolves the Greater Vancouver Regional Hospital District and transfers its assets: 15 acres in Surrey to the South Fraser Health Region, the Tilbury Laundry and adjacent land to the Vancouver/Richmond Health Board, a parkade to Vancouver General Hospital, and the rest of its assets and liabilities to the government

events.interpretation_notes: Effective 1 January 1999; approved 17 December 1998. Four recipient groups, not a merger into one health body. Whether either reversion happened is not known. The district was incorporated 29 June 1967 (OIC 2131/1967).
